Welcome. Imagine cruising down a stretch of American highway, the radio buzzing with classic riffs—and every mile marker holds a story, a secret, or a memory that just won't let go. Have you ever wondered why certain songs, certain moments, or even places where legends took their last breaths, seem to echo inside us long after the music fades?
Together, we’re about to set off on a journey that’s part road trip, part soul search, and part love letter to the raw mythology of rock and roll. In his book, Killing Yourself to Live: 85% of a True Story, Chuck Klosterman invites us to ride shotgun as he weaves together the wild tales of music’s brightest—and sometimes most tragic—icons, with his own tangled memories and bittersweet reflections.
Get ready to explore how the stories we tell about loss and fame might just reveal what it means to be alive. We’ll dive into moments where heartbreak meets humor, and nostalgia collides with the strange magic of pop culture. Along the way, we’ll meet strangers, revisit old flames, and uncover how music, memory, and mortality all intertwine. So, let’s buckle up—because this isn’t just about the places we go, but about the connections we crave and the meaning we’re all searching for.
